context: linux-x1 reproduced the FWS arm and found every phase, at every setting, exactly 16 bins lower than windows-desk - while the within-FWS site separation was identical (144 bins at FWS 4) and the peak magnitudes agreed to 0.1 codes
method: one capture, analysis start shifted by hand. Nothing about the board or the image changes; only where the fold begins.
findings: the reported phase shifts by exactly HALF the sample shift - pair_fold differences within pairs, so two samples are one bin
the peak magnitude is unchanged at +11.72 in every case: the artifact is identical and only its reported position moves
so a 16-bin bench-to-bench offset is 32 samples of capture-start difference, and needs no board, silicon or timing difference to explain it
why_this_is_the_likely_explanation: linux-x1 measured the peak magnitudes agreeing to 0.1 codes across two boards, two hosts and two rooms. A real difference in when the DAC timer and the ADC trigger are armed changes the MAGNITUDE as well - that is what the FWS arm demonstrates, where magnitude moves with phase. A constant phase offset with identical magnitude is the signature of a reporting offset, not of a physical one.

falsifiable_prediction.prediction: linux-x1's ps._index_at(CH_A0, SETTLE_US) mod 512 should be 32 samples from 480 - that is 448, or 0 if the offset runs the other way. If it is neither, this explanation is wrong and the offset is physical after all.

not_claimed: that the offset IS the window start - only that a 32-sample window difference is sufficient and that the magnitude agreement points away from a physical cause
